QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_18

question.text: Daily standard deviation of Cat III fund returns is 0.80%. Assuming 252 trading days per year, what is the annualised volatility?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Annualised σ = daily σ × √252 = 0.80% × 15.874 = 12.699% ≈ 12.70%. This is the standard square-root-of-time scaling assuming iid returns. **The Trap:** 9.80% uses √150. 2.02% uses √6.25. 201.60% multiplies by 252 (no square root). **Cross-Exam Context:** VIII Equity Derivatives tests same formula in options-vol context. XIX-E uses it for Cat III fund risk reports. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** √T scaling breaks when returns autocorrelate (classic in illiquid side-pocket or credit-heavy books). Use a Newey-West correction if your daily returns show |ρ₁| > 0.15.
